source.title: Base LLMs refuse too
source.authors: Connor Kissane; robertzk; Arthur Conmy; Neel Nanda

record.file_problem: The post text is present, but plotted values in referenced figures are not included in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: It applies the difference-in-mean refusal direction and the original-style activation ablation and addition, testing these interventions on base models and a chat model.
record.gate_note: The study states that steering increases refusal and ablation reduces it; the linked chart values themselves are unavailable in the supplied text. The mean refusal rates are reported explicitly. No rows are made from cited results or from values used only to select an intervention.
record.test_reason: It uses Arditi et al.'s difference-in-means direction, ablation at all layers, addition at the extraction layer, and a refusal-phrase score. It applies them to three base models and their chat versions, and transfers directions between base and chat. Its results bear on V1 (in base models), V6 (base↔chat transfer) and V7 (whether a removable direction exists before chat fine-tuning, and whether that differs by pretraining).
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is mostly right, with one refinement. Base models already refuse. In Qwen 1.5 0.5B and Gemma 2 9B the Arditi direction mediates refusal in both base and chat models, so fine-tuning reinforces existing circuitry. LLaMA 1 7B differs: addition still transfers, but ablation fails on the base model with either direction. Vicuna is bypassed only with its own chat-derived direction. The authors suggest chat fine-tuning changes LLaMA's mechanisms more, and that its base refusal may not be single-direction. They say the pre/post-ChatGPT explanation is not conclusive.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the difference in mean activations between harmful and harmless instructions and ablates across every layer and token position. It also adds the direction only at its extraction layer. It transfers directions between base and chat models and uses 32 instruction pairs; subjects include base models as well as chat models.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model family and by whether the direction is extracted from the base or chat model. Base-model prompting is model-specific: Qwen uses its chat template, Gemma uses a modified template, and LLaMA 1 is evaluated without the Vicuna system prompt. The post cautions that small prompt edits can substantially affect base-model refusal rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Base models with no chat fine-tuning already refuse 48% of harmful and 3% of harmless requests, against 90% and 3% for their chat versions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal behaviour partly arises during pretraining; chat fine-tuning raises its rate rather than creating it.

record.peer_reviewed: Alignment Forum post; the authors describe the work as ongoing research and say it will be fully reviewed when developed into a paper.
record.problems: Only three models are investigated. The refusal measure checks for common refusal phrases and may miss refusals, especially in less constrained base models. The authors note substantial prompt sensitivity and limited transparency about Qwen and Gemma pretraining. No general-capability preservation check or uncertainty estimates are reported. Per-condition plotted values are absent from the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: None. Per-model plotted values were unavailable in the supplied text, so the relevant conditions are retained as figure-only rows rather than omitted.

untested.parts: Whether general capabilities are preserved after ablation or addition. Chat models other than Vicuna are not ablated in this post. No per-model numbers are given in the text.
Not tested: no weight-edit or abliteration result on a released model.

Not tested. The ablation failure in LLaMA 1 base is not followed by any search for an affine, cone or multi-direction structure. The authors speculate there may be a separate 'incompetent refusal' direction.
Transfer across languages is not tested. Transfer is tested only within three base/chat pairs.
Training is not manipulated. The pretraining contrast is confounded with model capability and pretraining method; the authors say this is not conclusive.

missing.what: Aggregate harmful-request refusal rate after steering base models with the refusal direction: over 88%. It is mentioned in row notes but recorded as no row's value.
missing.locator: Results, 'Eliciting more base model refusals with steering vectors'

missing.what: Qualitative finding that steering LLaMA 1 base with its own direction yields 'incompetent refusals' (claims of inability), unlike steering with the Vicuna direction.

record.verdict_notes: This is an Alignment Forum post by Kissane, Krzyzanowski, Conmy and Nanda, not one of the originals. All direction-intervention values are figure-only; states rest on the authors' text. The reader's V4 'supports' was dropped because a failed ablation does not establish an alternative geometry. The reader's V6 limits_scope reason misstated r23: the Vicuna chat direction does work on Vicuna. The reader's overlapping V7 supports and limits_scope labels were merged into one label. Commenters note that the Qwen and Gemma 'base' models had filtered or synthetic instruction data in pretraining, which blurs the base/chat split. A comment reports Pythia 12B refuses 13% of harmful requests, with no direction test.

versions.untested_parts: General capability preservation is not evaluated. Addition is applied at the direction's extraction layer, not every layer; most tested subjects are base models rather than safety-trained chat models.
No released-model weight edit or practical abliteration result is reported; the post describes activation ablation and cites another work for its mathematical equivalence to weight editing.
No jailbreak suppression of the direction or training against its ablation is tested.
The post does not identify or test an affine, cone-shaped, or multiple-direction representation; it reports a single-direction ablation failure for LLaMA 1 7B.
No separate harmfulness judgment and refusal-decision representations are tested.
Transfer across languages and between base and instruct models beyond the named model pairs is not tested.
Training data and procedures are not manipulated or systematically compared; the proposed explanation for differences by training period is not established causally.

source_check.notes: The pack gave no [lN] ids, so label_ids l1–l5 follow pack order. The citation block lists Kissane, Krzyzanowski, Conmy and Nanda (2024-09-29). Nanda co-authored Arditi et al., so independence counts are affected. The only numbers in the text are aggregates: base 48%/3% (harmful/harmless), chat 90%/3%, steered base over 88% harmful. There is no random-direction control, and the authors warn base refusal rates are prompt-sensitive. Commenters note that Qwen/Gemma pretraining data is filtered or synthetic.

statements.problem: Accurate for this study. The cited rows (r5, r7, r11) cover only addition; the ablation rows r17 and r19 are not cited.

statements.correction: lw:YWo2: Qwen 1.5 0.5B and Gemma 2 9B base: addition and ablation both work (figure-only). LLaMA 1 7B base: addition induces refusal (r9, r10, r15, r16); ablation fails (r21, r22). No random-direction control; per-model values figure-only.
statements.problem: This study tests both operations on base checkpoints outside Llama/OLMo/Qwen3-8B-Base (Qwen 1.5 0.5B, Gemma 2 9B), so the gap as worded is contradicted. The statement also leaves out that this study has its own LLaMA 1 7B base rows. The 'no random-direction control' point is right.

statements.correction: Earlier-stage-to-later failure: r24 (LLaMA 1 7B base direction does not remove Vicuna 7B v1.1 refusal). r22 is the reverse direction (Vicuna to LLaMA base ablation fails). Vicuna-direction addition into LLaMA base works (r10, r16). All figure-only.
statements.problem: r22 is a chat (Vicuna) direction failing in the earlier-stage base model, the reverse of 'earlier stage fails in later model'. Only r24 fits that heading. The record's verdict for this pair is limits_scope, since chat-to-base addition works (r10, r16).
Accurate for this study (chat-to-base, model-specific templates, refusal-phrase score, figure-only).

statements.correction: lw:YWo2 says the ablation is 'mathematically equivalent to editing the model's weights'. Base-direction ablation in Vicuna 7B v1.1 does not remove refusal (r24, figure-only).
statements.problem: Literally true: they use activation ablation. But the authors state their all-layer ablation is mathematically equivalent to weight orthogonalization, so r24 is in effect a base-to-instruct weight-edit test, and it fails.
